flagship.headline: Jimi Hendrix rings in 1970 with Band of Gypsys at the Fillmore East
flagship.summary_line_1: Jimi Hendrix and his Band of Gypsys played two shows at the Fillmore East in New York on December 31, 1969, before a sold-out crowd of 2,639, with the Voices of East Harlem opening, according to the Official Jimi Hendrix Site.
flagship.summary_line_2: The band played the same stage twice more on January 1, 1970, and the clip below is Machine Gun from the Fillmore East run, from Hendrix's Topic channel.

events.headline: Jimi Hendrix rings in 1970 with Band of Gypsys at the Fillmore East
events.summary_line_1: Jimi Hendrix and his Band of Gypsys played two shows at the Fillmore East in New York on December 31, 1969, before a sold-out crowd of 2,639, with the Voices of East Harlem opening, according to the Official Jimi Hendrix Site.
events.summary_line_2: The band played the same stage twice more on January 1, 1970, and the clip below is Machine Gun from the Fillmore East run, from Hendrix's Topic channel.

events.headline: The Monkees reach No. 1 on the Hot 100 with I'm a Believer
events.summary_line_1: The Monkees' I'm a Believer climbed from No. 3 to No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 dated December 31, 1966, after entering the chart at No. 44 on December 10.
events.summary_line_2: Written by Neil Diamond, it stayed at the top for seven weeks, according to the Songfacts calendar, and the clip below is the song from the band's Topic channel.

events.headline: The Royal Guardsmen reach their peak with Snoopy vs. the Red Baron
events.summary_line_1: The Royal Guardsmen's Snoopy vs. the Red Baron rose to its No. 2 peak on the Billboard Hot 100 dated December 31, 1966, after entering the chart at No. 30 on December 17.
events.summary_line_2: Only the Monkees' I'm a Believer stood above it that week, and the clip below is the song from the group's Topic channel.

events.headline: Nancy Sinatra reaches her peak with Sugar Town
events.summary_line_1: Nancy Sinatra's Sugar Town rose to its No. 5 peak on the Billboard Hot 100 dated December 31, 1966, after entering the chart at No. 83 on November 19.
events.summary_line_2: She was the daughter of Frank Sinatra, and the clip below is the song from her Topic channel.

events.headline: The Temptations reach their peak with (I Know) I'm Losing You
events.summary_line_1: The Temptations' (I Know) I'm Losing You rose to its No. 8 peak on the Billboard Hot 100 dated December 31, 1966, after entering the chart at No. 79 on November 19.
events.summary_line_2: The clip below is the song from the group's Topic channel.

events.headline: The Yardbirds reach their peak with Happenings Ten Years Time Ago
events.summary_line_1: The Yardbirds' Happenings Ten Years Time Ago rose to its No. 30 peak on the Billboard Hot 100 dated December 31, 1966, after entering the chart at No. 99 on November 26.
events.summary_line_2: The clip below is the song from the band's Topic channel.

events.headline: The Spencer Davis Group debut on the Hot 100 with Gimme Some Lovin'
events.summary_line_1: The Spencer Davis Group's Gimme Some Lovin' entered the Billboard Hot 100 dated December 31, 1966 at No. 100.
events.summary_line_2: The clip below is the song from the group's Topic channel.

events.headline: The Beatles play the sixth night of Another Beatles Christmas Show
events.summary_line_1: The Beatles played two shows at the Hammersmith Odeon in London on December 31, 1964, at 6:15 pm and 8:45 pm, the sixth night of Another Beatles Christmas Show, per the Paul McCartney Project.
events.summary_line_2: Paul McCartney and George Harrison then went to EMI producer Norman Newell's New Year's Eve party in London, and the clip below is I Feel Fine, the band's current single, from their Topic channel.

events.headline: The Beatles play the Astoria Theatre on New Year's Eve
events.summary_line_1: The Beatles played the Astoria Theatre in Finsbury Park, London, on December 31, 1963, part of The Beatles Christmas Show, which ran from December 24 to January 11, per the Paul McCartney Project.
events.summary_line_2: Their She Loves You had been released in the UK on August 23, 1963, and the clip below is that song from the band's Topic channel.

events.headline: Jerry Garcia and Bob Weir meet in a Palo Alto music store
events.summary_line_1: Jerry Garcia was waiting for banjo pupils at Dana Morgan's music store in Palo Alto on New Year's Eve 1963 when 15-year-old Bob Weir heard him playing and walked in, according to Palo Alto History.
events.summary_line_2: They jammed and decided to start a jug band, Mother McCree's Uptown Jug Champions, a step toward the Grateful Dead, and the clip below is Viola Lee Blues from the Dead's Topic channel.

events.headline: The Beatles play their last night at the Star-Club in Hamburg
events.summary_line_1: The Beatles played the Star-Club in Hamburg on December 31, 1962, the thirteenth and final date of their third residency there, per the Paul McCartney Project and the Beatles Bible.
events.summary_line_2: Their next single, Please Please Me, came out in the UK on January 11, 1963, and the clip below is that song from the band's Topic channel.

events.headline: The Beach Boys play the Ritchie Valens Memorial Dance as the Beach Boys
events.summary_line_1: The Beach Boys played the Ritchie Valens Memorial Dance at the Municipal Auditorium in Long Beach, California, on December 31, 1961, on a bill with the Ike and Tina Turner Revue, per Becoming the Beach Boys.
events.summary_line_2: They played three songs including Surfin', and the clip below is that song from the band's Topic channel.

events.headline: The Beatles close out 1960 at the Casbah Coffee Club
events.summary_line_1: The Beatles played the Casbah Coffee Club in Liverpool on December 31, 1960, their second show there in two weeks after December 17, per the Paul McCartney Project.
events.summary_line_2: Their first record, My Bonnie, would be made in Hamburg with Tony Sheridan in 1961, and the clip below is that song from the band's Topic channel.
